title: Affine Schemes and the Structure Sheaf

items.title: The locally ringed spectrum of a commutative ring
items.strategy: Fix the topological spectrum from the prior Zariski page and name its intended locally ringed-space enhancement; the sheaf itself is constructed in the next items.

items.title: The localization presheaf on principal distinguished opens
items.strategy: On the distinguished-open basis set O(D(f)) = A_f and define restriction maps by the universal property of localization.

items.title: Localization sections and their restrictions are independent of a basic-open presentation
items.strategy: Use the localization universal property and the D(f)-cover/refinement facts to compare presentations; prove the finite compatible-family gluing required on the basis.

items.title: The localization construction extends to the structure sheaf on Spec A
items.strategy: Apply the basis sheaf criterion to the preceding lemma, then use the sheaf-on-a-basis extension theorem; identify the resulting stalk maps as local in the next theorem.

items.title: Sections and restrictions on distinguished opens of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Transport the basis construction through sheafification/extension to prove Γ(D(f), O) ≅ A_f, including the canonical restriction maps for D(g) contained in D(f).

items.title: The stalk of the affine structure sheaf at a prime is A_p
items.strategy: Compute the stalk as the filtered colimit over the distinguished neighborhoods of p and use the localization universal property to obtain the canonical isomorphism.

items.title: Spec A with its structure sheaf is a locally ringed space
items.strategy: Combine the stalk computation with the prior fact that A_p is local, so every stalk of O_Spec A is a local ring.

items.title: The residue field at a point of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Define κ(p) = O_p/m_p and record its canonical affine presentation A_p/pA_p ≅ Frac(A/p).

items.title: Global functions on Spec A recover A
items.strategy: Specialize the distinguished-open section calculation to D(1) = Spec A and track the canonical isomorphism Γ(Spec A, O) ≅ A.

items.title: A principal localization identifies its spectrum with a distinguished open
items.strategy: Use the prior localization-spectrum homeomorphism and the affine structure-sheaf section calculation to upgrade Spec(A_f) ≅ D(f) to an isomorphism of locally ringed spaces.

items.title: Affine schemes and their coordinate rings
items.strategy: Define an affine scheme as a locally ringed space isomorphic to Spec A, with the coordinate ring Γ(X, O_X) identified by the preceding theorem.

items.title: The affine-scheme morphism induced by a ring homomorphism
items.strategy: For φ : A → B, define the contraction map Spec B → Spec A and the compatible map on localization sections; state the local-stalk criterion that will be proved next.

items.title: The stalk maps of a morphism induced by a ring map are local
items.strategy: Identify the stalk map at q with A_{φ⁻¹q} → B_q and check that the inverse image of the maximal ideal is the maximal ideal using contraction of primes.

items.title: Affine schemes are contravariantly equivalent to commutative rings
items.strategy: Use global sections for one composite and show a scheme morphism to an affine target is determined by its global-ring map, with the induced localization maps giving the other composite.

items.title: Affine-scheme isomorphisms are exactly coordinate-ring isomorphisms in reverse direction
items.strategy: Reflect isomorphisms through the preceding anti-equivalence.

items.title: Closed points of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Define a closed scheme point topologically and translate it on Spec A to maximal ideals using the established Zariski correspondence.

items.title: Classical k-points give closed points over an algebraically closed field
items.strategy: For a reduced finite-type k-algebra with k algebraically closed, invoke the affine-algebra maximal-ideal correspondence and distinguish these k-points from all scheme points.

items.title: Generic points of irreducible closed subsets
items.strategy: Define generic point by closure and identify V(p) with its prime point in an affine spectrum.

items.title: Every irreducible closed subset of an affine spectrum has a unique generic point
items.strategy: Use the prime/irreducible-closed-subset correspondence and the T0 property to prove existence and uniqueness separately.

items.title: Reduced affine schemes
items.strategy: Define reducedness by a reduced coordinate ring and record its invariance under affine-scheme isomorphism via the anti-equivalence.

items.title: Integral affine schemes
items.strategy: Define integrality by a nonzero integral-domain coordinate ring and state the equivalent nonempty, reduced, irreducible affine criterion using prior topological algebra.

items.title: An affine nilpotent thickening
items.strategy: For a nilpotent ideal I in A, define the affine morphism Spec(A/I) → Spec A and record that it is a homeomorphism on underlying spaces while retaining different structure sheaves.

items.title: The functor of points of an affine scheme
items.strategy: Define h_X(R) = Hom_Sch(Spec R, X), contravariantly in rings, and identify h_Spec A(R) with Hom_CRing(A, R) through the affine anti-equivalence.

items.title: An affine scheme is determined by its functor of points
items.strategy: Apply the Yoneda lemma to the representable functors of points and translate the resulting natural isomorphism into an affine-scheme isomorphism.

items.title: The affine scheme of dual numbers
items.strategy: Define D_k = Spec(k[ε]/(ε²)) and flag it as the basic one-point nonreduced affine model whose details are worked in the companion.

items.title: Every distinguished open of an affine spectrum is quasi-compact
items.strategy: Identify D(f) with Spec(A_f) and transport quasi-compactness from the prior prime-spectrum theorem.

items.title: Every affine scheme is quasi-compact
items.strategy: Apply the preceding result to D(1) = Spec A; retain the library's stated choice principle inherited by prime-spectrum compactness.

items.title: Contravariance reverses coordinates and scheme points are not only classical points
items.strategy: Synthesize the anti-equivalence, the closed/generic-point distinction, and the residue-field convention without adding a new theorem.

title: Affine Schemes and the Structure Sheaf — Examples

items.title: The spectrum of a field is a one-point affine scheme
items.strategy: Compute the sole prime, its local ring and its global sections directly from the field-localization formulas.

items.title: The zero ring has empty spectrum
items.strategy: Use the unital convention to show that no prime ideal can be proper, then record the empty affine scheme and its zero global ring.

items.title: Spec Z has one generic point and closed prime-number points
items.strategy: Classify the primes of Z, then apply the closed-point and generic-point descriptions to separate (0) from (p).

items.title: Dual numbers give a one-point nonreduced affine scheme
items.strategy: Show that (ε) is the only prime of k[ε]/(ε²), while ε remains a nonzero nilpotent; compare its underlying point with its residue field.

items.title: The spectrum of a product ring is a disjoint union
items.strategy: Classify prime ideals of A × B using the two complementary idempotents and match the localization sheaves to obtain Spec(A × B) ≅ Spec A ⊔ Spec B.

items.title: A basic open of the affine line is affine
items.strategy: For A¹_k = Spec k[t], calculate D(t) as Spec k[t,t⁻¹] through the principal-localization open immersion.

items.title: The underlying topological space does not determine a scheme
items.strategy: Compare Spec k with the dual-numbers spectrum: both have one point, but their local rings and reducedness differ.

items.title: Relative points of the affine line are elements of a test k-algebra
items.strategy: For a specified k-algebra R, apply the polynomial-ring universal property to identify Hom_k-Alg(k[t], R) with the underlying set of R; via the affine anti-equivalence these are the maps Spec R → A¹_k compatible with Spec R → Spec k.

items.title: A nonclosed scheme point need not be a k-valued coordinate
items.strategy: Use the generic point (0) of Spec k[t]: its residue field is k(t), so it is not represented by evaluation at an element of k.
